A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. All pages, including appendices, support comparison through text extraction and visual inspection. Renumbered tables and relocated rationale examples can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of seven LLMs on four mathematical reasoning datasets, prompting comparisons, and human evaluation of generated rationales.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds confidence intervals, annotator-dispersion statistics, and ROUGE analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the same prompt construction, example-generation procedures, and task instructions. No algorithm, model component, or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use GSM8K, ASDiv, AQuA, and PRM800K for the same mathematical tasks, plus GSM8K rationale evaluation. The added analyses use existing coverage.

E2.justification: CoT and explicit learning remain the main comparators, with CoT+ and CoT-2 retained in the corresponding supplementary comparisons. The new ROUGE analysis reuses existing prompting strategies.

E3.justification: v3 adds ROUGE-1 and ROUGE-L recall metrics to the rationale-similarity evaluation. Existing benchmark metrics, models, data preparation, prompt sizes, and decoding settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 tests rationale similarity using additional ROUGE metrics and examines dispersion in annotators' quality-label proportions. Existing context-length controls, human evaluations, and representative rationale cases are retained; the cases move into Section 5.2.

E5.justification: v3 introduces a comprehensive 95% t-based confidence-interval analysis for the main comparisons (Appendix D/Table 5), alongside MAD-based reporting of annotator-label dispersion. This substantially expands statistical reporting beyond v2. Both versions report five runs; no increase is established.

E6.justification: Retained benchmark, CoT+/CoT-2, human-rating, and bigram-similarity scores are unchanged. New results include confidence intervals, MAD within 0.05, and Table 8 ROUGE-1/ROUGE-L scores: CoT 0.18/0.13, implicit 0.26/0.19, and explicit 0.19/0.14. The ROUGE prose contradicts this ranking, and some new intervals conflict with Table 1.

T1.justification: The prompt definitions and equations remain equivalent. Neither version introduces theoretical proofs, and v3's descriptions of established statistical and similarity measures add no new formal results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: implicit learning outperforms the compared prompting approaches, incorrect answers provide useful information, and explicit rationales can over-constrain models.

C2.justification: v3 interprets low MAD as agreement on overall rationale quality and presents ROUGE as corroborating explicit-rationale overfitting. That ROUGE interpretation conflicts with Table 8. Existing limitations concerning mathematical domains and extension to fine-tuning remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 replaces the OpenReview attachment reference with a GitHub repository pointer for examples across all datasets. Existing model identifiers, hyperparameters, data-preparation instructions, and displayed prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Lampinen et al. (2022), acknowledging broader prior investigation of explanations in context in the limitations discussion. Other reference changes largely update publication metadata for already cited works.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized copyedits and author/contact updates, integrates the former representative-rationales appendix into Section 5.2, and adds statistical and ROUGE appendix sections. The overall narrative and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds confidence-interval and ROUGE tables, gives Figure 4 a taller plotting area, and relocates existing rationale boxes into the main text. Other figures and tables are retained, with corresponding renumbering and page reflow.

improvement.justification: The repository pointer and integrated examples improve usability, but new evidence introduces material inconsistencies. Table 5 gives WizardLM's CoT AQuA-solving interval as 40.87–41.13 although the unchanged Table 1 score is 59.1. Table 8 ranks implicit prompting highest in ROUGE while the text claims explicit is highest. These errors weaken evidential reliability, outweighing the limited presentation benefits; the original experiments remain intact.
